ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 1/4: DECISIONS
Gathered 2026-08-03 by a read-only research pass over all 40 epic descendants plus 7b22, ed82, a574
(which are NOT in list-descendants — they are detached; see Part 4). Code citations were opened and
line-verified at HEAD 6c390d7a0a. Raw ticket dumps: /tmp/adrsrc/*.txt, notes /tmp/agent{A,D,E,F}.md.
READ PART 4 FIRST IF YOU ARE WRITING THE ADR: two of this ticket's own premises are FALSE.

## THE SEAM
D1 The seam is pydantic-ai's `provider_factory` hook, not a rebar invention. 7468: "Upstream directs
   user-configurable-provider apps to exactly this hook (pydantic-ai#1343) rather than patching
   `infer_provider`, so rebar depends on a supported contract." providers.py:132-176; sole call site
   runner.py:350.
D2 It is a per-run SESSION object, not a bare function, because of client teardown: "The hook's return
   type carries a `Provider` only, with no channel for the retrying httpx.AsyncClient." One session per
   run(), never shared, so `_closeables` needs no locking. providers.py:74, :102, :309-321, :323-327.
D3 S1 landed as a PURE RELOCATION before any new provider used it, so Bedrock/OpenAI were additive
   registrations rather than surgery on run().
D4 Builder BODIES live in leaf modules; the REGISTRY and every call site live in providers.py.
   Registry providers.py:106-109; openai registered conditionally :117-118, :163-164. Bodies
   anthropic_model.py:160, bedrock_model.py:88, providers.py:256-290.

## CAPABILITIES
D5 Capability decisions read ModelProfile, NEVER a provider-name string. capabilities.py:1;
   structured.py:43-60 branches on caps.native_structured_output at :58; cache_settings_for dispatches
   solely on caps.prompt_cache_style. `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` is GONE (grep: zero hits).
D6 prompt_cache_style is derived from profile FIELD PRESENCE, not concrete type — a hard constraint.
   f184: "the attested v6 plan said prompt_cache_style is derived from the profile's CONCRETE TYPE
   (isinstance BedrockModelProfile). That is unimplementable in CI. BedrockModelProfile is exported only
   from pydantic_ai.models.bedrock, which imports botocore at module top; there is no SDK-free
   pydantic_ai.profiles.bedrock; and boto3 appears in pyproject.toml ONLY under the reviewbot extra. An
   isinstance check would break the stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract AND fail CI."
   capabilities.py:209-248.
D7 TWO override tables, deliberately apart, both membership-keyed. `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` is an ORDERED
   TUPLE of (predicate, overrides), "deliberately NOT a dict keyed by provider name, for two reasons: a
   name key would reintroduce exactly the string matching this story exists to remove, and it could not
   express the single rule below, which must span two different HOSTS of the same model family."
   capabilities.py:138-153. `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` keys on the exact full model id,
   :186-206. 2932 on why separate: "f184's keys on capability shape (what kind of model is this), this
   one keys on a specific model's API defect (this exact id rejects a parameter)." And why f184 was not
   widened: "f184 is closed and its plan-review attestation is signed... widening that signature would
   silently redefine a shipped, signed contract from a downstream leaf. The rule is that the parent wins."
D8 `_is_claude` keys on bedrock_thinking_variant == "anthropic"; BOTH arms required. f184:
   "Bedrock-hosted Claude's profile is a BedrockModelProfile, NOT an AnthropicModelProfile (verified —
   sibling subclasses), so an isinstance(AnthropicModelProfile) test alone would miss the very models this
   epic exists to support." And: "this is a capability FIELD READ whose value happens to be a string enum
   — materially different from resolved.startswith('anthropic')."
D9 supports_thinking goes on the record NOW, before anything signs it, though nothing branches on it:
   "the signed record must already state whether the model that produced each historical verdict was
   CAPABLE of thinking, because that fact cannot be reconstructed later... Adding the field after S5 ships
   is also strictly more expensive." Labelled "a deliberate, documented exception to 'no field without a
   consumer'." Same argument reused for supports_temperature on 343b.

## THE REGISTRY-MEMBERSHIP QUALIFIER
D10 Qualification by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, matching OSS consensus. 7b22: "The shape test works for the ids
   we have, but it answers the wrong question. It asks 'does this prefix LOOK like a provider name?' when
   the answer needed is 'IS this prefix a provider name?'" Consensus: LangChain's
   `model.split(":",1)[0] in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`, LiteLLM's `provider_list`, pydantic-ai's
   `infer_provider_class` raising. Code config.py:214-241 (KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES), decider :244-261.
D11 The set is a LITERAL of plain strings — no imports, no lazy loading: "split_provider_qualifier runs
   during config resolution, where the optional [agents] extra may not be importable at all."
D12 NO name is grandfathered; neither `test` nor `google_genai` is a member. Deciding probe against
   pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1: infer_model("test:foo") -> ValueError: Unknown provider: test;
   infer_model("google_genai:gemini-2.0") -> Unknown provider: google_genai. "Granting either name
   membership would make rebar MORE permissive than the library it wraps, which is backwards."
D13 Two paths, deliberately ASYMMETRIC: strict on a CONFIGURED provider, permissive on an unrecognized
   INLINE prefix — because "anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0".partition(":") yields a prefix that
   is by construction not a provider name. "Falling back to 'not qualified' is the only answer that keeps
   a colon-bearing model id intact." Configured-provider validation model_classes.py:247-252.
D14 GUARD ORDER is the real fix, and NEVER silently fall back. 03b0: "an explicitly configured provider is
   checked FIRST, before the model string is scanned at all." Policy verbatim: "GRACEFUL FALLBACK IS THE
   WRONG CHOICE HERE... its origin was 41 of 42 calls silently reaching direct Anthropic... Fail closed
   (already) + fail fast (to add); never fall back."
D15 `:` stays the separator. "pydantic-ai's own KnownModelName contains TWO-COLON entries
   ('bedrock:anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0')... no project was found regretting a separator."
   Direction of travel worth an ADR line: "pydantic-ai REMOVED bare-name inference in v2.0.0b1."

## NATIVE BEDROCK
D16 Native BedrockConverseModel + BedrockProvider, ambient AWS credential chain, NO rebar-managed key.
   bedrock_model.py:41-88; config.py:450-453 records there is deliberately no Bedrock credential field.
D17 Documented default `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` — an INFERENCE-PROFILE id, because on-demand ids
   are not invokable, and it is the MEASURED-caching id. bedrock_model.py:38, ValidationException :17-20.
D18 Bedrock sets exactly TWO cache breakpoints for parity, not three: "An earlier draft named a third
   (bedrock_cache_messages); that is REJECTED for parity... Enabling message caching on Bedrock alone
   would make it cache MORE than Anthropic." LATER SUPERSEDED ON BOTH ARMS BY dd27 — see D25.
D19 temperature is carried as a CAPABILITY via a second exact-id table: "_REBAR_OVERRIDES predicates
   receive only the ModelProfile, and BedrockModelProfile carries NO per-model identifier, so the only
   predicate expressible would strip temperature from us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 too — the
   measured-good default." On the apparent relapse: "This is model-id matching, and that is deliberate,
   not a relapse... recording a known per-model API defect is a different thing, and it is what
   pydantic-ai itself does." DENYLIST over allowlist: "an unknown-but-affected model then fails LOUDLY,
   whereas an allowlist would silently drop temperature from an unknown-but-fine model."
D20 Error-CONTENT-keyed translation in failure.py, never a provider branch. Three-conjunct predicate
   (400-or-ValidationException AND a sampling-param name AND a rejection word) "so an unrelated 400 is
   NOT swallowed."
D21 The Bedrock region pre-check raises a typed LLMConfigError rather than inventing a default.
   bedrock_model.py:67-88.

## TIERS AND VERDICT PROVENANCE
D22 ADDITIVE sibling `provider_provenance` object; the `model` string is untouched. "Additive-only is
   deliberate: it makes this a backward-compatible payload change, so an older reader ignores the new key
   and no store-compatibility gate or migration is required." capabilities.py:395-446; stamped
   runner.py:405-407; persisted completion_sidecar.py:213/:231, plan_review/sidecar.py:637,
   code_review/sidecar.py:106.
D23 SIGN ON EVERY TIER; give the consumer a lever instead of a refusal: "a contributor running Ollama can
   still exercise the gates, which matters for the OSS on-ramp."
D24 REUSE the capability record, never recompute; `.hostname` never `.netloc`; OMIT the key where no model
   ran. "Provenance must stamp THAT record, not call capabilities_for again — a second resolution can
   silently diverge from the record that actually drove the run." Guard
   test_verdict_provenance.py:115. Credential trap named: "runner.py:650 uses parsed.netloc, which
   RETAINS user:secret@." Omission: "A cfg-derived record at a site where nothing ran would reproduce the
   EXACT defect this record exists to fix."

## PROMPT CACHING
D25 A THIRD breakpoint on the AGENTIC path only, with DIFFERENT keys per arm (anthropic_cache=True /
   bedrock_cache_messages=True). capabilities.py:454, :503-514. "System-only is the documented minimum for
   a STATIC-PROMPT workload; it is not the shape for an agent." Budget: pydantic-ai's
   _limit_cache_points sets MAX_CACHE_POINTS = 3 if automatic_caching else 4; this puts rebar at 3.
D26 Per-model cache floor from Anthropic's PUBLISHED table; empirical brackets are VERIFICATION ONLY.
   e3cd: "Anthropic's PUBLISHED table, not the brackets: platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/
   prompt-caching, section 'Minimum cacheable prompt length', read 2026-08-02. The ticket's two
   independent measurements were used only to VERIFY it, and all three agree." 13 entries at
   512/1024/2048/4096, capabilities.py:68-84. Rejected: a single global — "The published table is NOT
   monotonic across generations, which is exactly why one global could not express it."
   THIS IS THE GOLD STANDARD FOR CITATION HYGIENE IN THIS EPIC — published URL + read date, brackets
   explicitly demoted.
D27 Bedrock ids are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the floor table: "Anthropic's table states these minimums
   apply on every platform EXCEPT Amazon Bedrock, which publishes its own. rebar has measured none of
   Bedrock's, so a Bedrock model falls through rather than being assigned a guessed number."
D28 Compare the MARKED PREFIX, not total input_tokens; and DO NOT add the floor to the signed record:
   "Adding a 5th key to its capabilities record would change the bytes of already-signed gate verdicts;
   the floor is a published property of the model, recoverable from the recorded model id."

## MODEL CLASSES AND PER-PASS CONFIG
D29 THREE capability classes are the universal interface; internals never name a model id. "Each class is
   a config SLOT the operator fills... The three names are SLOTS the client fills, not presets rebar
   ships." Root cause: "one knob for four passes. REBAR_LLM_MODEL is a single scalar, and a scalar cannot
   express a per-tier mapping." NOTE: no argument for the number THREE exists anywhere — see Part 4.
D30 KEYSTONE: class names are RESERVED VALUES in the existing model-string space — no schema change.
   "the DSL stays closed and its VALUE space gains three reserved words." model_classes.py:309-332.
D31 CORRECTION TO D30: there is NO single funnel — one FUNCTION, three CALL SITES. eb58 verbatim:
   "CORRECTION to the keystone decision — my 'ONE funnel' claim was WRONG... I proposed the exact cycle I
   had just prohibited." And: "What I gave up is the false claim that a single interception point exists.
   Pretending it did would have shipped a change where the step path resolved classes correctly and its
   tests passed, while ladders and verifiers silently passed the literal strings 'standard'/'frontier'
   through to a provider as if they were model ids."
D32 Secrets stay ENV-ONLY, deliberately diverging from LiteLLM: "LiteLLM puts api_key inline in
   litellm_params and rebar must not copy that." Enforced model_classes.py:80-83.
D33 Layering: tables merge recursively (leaf key wins); ARRAYS ARE REPLACED WHOLESALE. "a table-level
   replace would force CI to restate an entire class slot to change one field, which IS the duplication
   this pointer exists to avoid." And: "Appending is rejected because a chain that can only grow can never
   be shortened, reordered, or cleared by an environment." Precedence: CLI -c > env >
   REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE > discovered config file > built-in default.
D34 The env-var names are string LITERALS, not f-strings, each read through its own literal
   os.environ.get, because scripts/gen_env_registry.py statically scans for literal arguments — a
   formatted name would silently escape the documented registry. model_classes.py:99-104, nine names
   :105-115.
D35 Per-step class assignments stated EXACTLY so no executor guesses; batch steps use a SINGLE-RUNG
   model_ladder. base->frontier; round_a/round_b->model_ladder:[frontier]; verify->standard;
   coach->standard. "A review round blocked twice on this being unspecified." Why not a step-level
   `model:` on a batch step: "A step-level model: on a batch: step is a SILENT NO-OP... Because model IS
   a legal step key, such a declaration VALIDATES and is then discarded — and a test asserting only that
   the YAML carries a class token would PASS while runtime behaviour was unchanged. An earlier version of
   this very table made that mistake." Why ONE rung: "A ladder escalates per criterion, so the model that
   actually answers a given criterion is NOT determinate."
D36 REBAR_LLM_MODEL is DEPRECATED with a migration window, not a permanent alias: "There are few clients
   today and a single-scalar knob alongside a class model is precisely the ambiguity this work removes."
   During the window it fans out to all three classes (docs/llm-framework.md:155-157).
D37 STANDING OPERATOR RULE (afeb): "For REVIEWS, Pass-2 and Pass-4 are DESIGNED to use a sonnet-equivalent
   model (the standard class), with LIMITED ESCAPE HATCHES for escalation to a higher class (frontier)."
   And: "the fix is NOT 'give these calls frontier' — the default for verification/judging work is
   standard. A site that needs frontier must justify it as an explicit, bounded escape hatch."
D38 RESTORATION (77ed): Pass-1 finder on frontier/opus; Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach on standard/sonnet.
   "That split is what _verifier_cfg was written to express, and its own docstring already asserts it...
   The docstring has simply been false since 2026-06-27. This is a RESTORATION, not a new preference."
D39 Single-call ops keep cfg.model; the class vocabulary exists for MULTI-pass gates. "rebar review is a
   SINGLE call: there is no 'here versus there' to differentiate." Cost of getting it wrong: "an operator
   who steers by setting the bare llm.model CONFIG-FILE key no longer steers rebar review at all."
D40 `self._config` is the FLOOR; `req.config` is the per-call OVERRIDE. THE EPIC'S SINGLE ROOT
   ARCHITECTURAL DEFECT was one line: runner.py:239 `cfg = self._config`. Shape decision: "Substitute into
   a COPY of the config, not a loose variable at the resolution point... Reading a separate model variable
   at _pai_model only would have left the provider session built for the FLOOR's provider."
D41 Escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary; escalation WINDOWS stay keyed on concrete model
   families. Provider-agreement rule: "providers differ on a HIGHER rung -> drop the rung... there is no
   honest target. Escalation stops and the existing too-big failure finding reports it — a visible outcome
   instead of a silent provider jump."
D42 Fix the CONSUMPTION of MODEL_LADDER, not the table. 1157: "Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 genuinely share a
   1M window. The table is honest; the ladder's USE of it is not." 48b3: "The two error directions are not
   symmetric. Under-blocking is silent: the review proceeds and truncates. Over-blocking is loud and
   actionable." Hence an unlocated window resolves to the ladder MINIMUM, and an unlocated primary to
   [model] not [] — "Returning [] would discard the single-criterion retry, which is the step that most
   often succeeds."

## BEST-EFFORT OPENAI-COMPATIBLE
D43 base_url is provider CONFIGURATION, not provider SELECTION.
D44 The openai builder is registered ONLY when cfg.base_url is set, and the reason does not rest on SDK
   absence: "with no base_url configured, rebar has NOTHING TO CONTRIBUTE to provider construction — no
   endpoint to inject, no key to place, no profile to override... rebar builds a provider only when it has
   configuration to apply." providers.py:110-118.
D45 The profile override rides the PROVIDER, not a model argument — forced by the seam: "rebar's factory
   hands back a Provider and pydantic-ai's infer_model constructs the model itself — so a model-level
   argument is unreachable from the seam." Justification: "the OpenAI profile describes OpenAI's HOSTED
   API. A custom base_url is by definition a different server... Withdrawing that one flag makes the
   plan's original claim true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by assumption."
D46 _pai_check_config VALIDATES instead of refusing. structured_run.py:576-597. Two remaining errors:
   api_key without base_url (:583-588), non-absolute base_url (:589-597).
D47 The optional SDKs are added to the `dev` extra ONLY, so CI can prove the story. Precedent: "dev
   already installs mcp, which is likewise an OPTIONAL runtime extra."

## STANDING OPERATOR DECISIONS RECORDED ON THE EPIC ITSELF
OD1 Keep stacking; ignore LOC-only Verified -1s; keep the TOP clean; operator manually overrides ancestors
   to submit. "Gerrit submitted_together confirms all 10 are one submit set with 5 submittable=False, so
   that override is genuinely required." Feature-branch verdict: "A feature branch was tried and DOES NOT
   HELP: submit requirements are inherited project-wide and CI fires on feature-branch changes, so it is
   strictly more review, not less. That branch has been deleted."
OD2 The per-FUNCTION length ratchet is REJECTED FOR NOW; SUPERSEDES ADR 0056's standing recommendation.
   MEASURED across 3,292 functions under src/rebar: 21 over 200 lines, 38 over 150, 62 over 120, 101 over
   100, ten worst spanning six subsystems. "Adopting it would either break the build in six subsystems at
   once or require an allowlist — and epic 716f deliberately DRAINED AND REMOVED the module-size
   allowlist." Consequence: "the module-level reworks are no longer a belt-and-braces mitigation — THEY
   ARE THE ONLY DEFENCE... the SEAM TEST becomes the substitute ratchet, and is now load-bearing."
OD3 Two orphaned open tickets (3768, 5e75) parented into the epic; "For 5e75 it is a REAL scope change."
   Load-bearing sequencing rule: "a ticket's PARENT is part of its material fingerprint... Parent before
   reviewing, never after."
OD4 THE BIG ONE — cross-model verdict comparison is OUT OF SCOPE. Operator ruling verbatim: "LLMs are
   non-deterministic. Expecting two runs to produce identical results is unrealistic AND BEYOND THE SCOPE
   OF THIS EPIC. The epic's scope is to ensure THE SAME PAYLOADS REACH THE LLM and THE LLM HAS THE SAME
   TOOLS AVAILABLE, regardless of model and provider. COMPARING MODELS AGAINST ONE ANOTHER IS OUT OF
   SCOPE." Best sentence for a "why the bar changed" section: "My earlier judgement — that the ticket
   could not honestly close as 'Bedrock cleared the bar' — was correct under the OLD criteria; the
   criteria were the problem, not the measurement."
OD5 Carry epic-level verdicts as COMMENTS, never description edits: "a description edit would be material
   and would invalidate this epic's plan-review attestation at the worst point in the sequence (the epic
   closes last)."

ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 2/4: REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, WITH THEIR EVIDENCE
This is the section the ADR most needs and the hardest to reconstruct later. Quotes are verbatim.

## 2.1 LiteLLM as an in-process SDK — REJECTED; a LiteLLM PROXY remains reachable
Epic 061c description verbatim: "Alternative rejected: LiteLLM as an in-process SDK (the aider /
OpenHands pattern). It buys 100+ providers for one dependency, but its normalization layer is documented
to drift on exactly what rebar depends on — prompt-cache semantics, tool-call shapes, and cost accounting
— and neither aider nor OpenHands escapes per-provider code anyway (OpenHands still carries a
model_features.py registry and two auto-detected completion modes). rebar chose pydantic-ai for weight and
structured-output reliability; adding LiteLLM in-process would duplicate its model layer. A LiteLLM PROXY
remains reachable through the best-effort OpenAI-compatible builder, so breadth is preserved without the
dependency."
IMPORTANT NUANCE — this is a PARTIAL rejection, not wholesale. LiteLLM's SHAPE was adopted where right:
  - eb58 cites LiteLLM's model_list alias / litellm_params shape as prior art for class slots.
  - 7b22 and 03b0 cite LiteLLM's provider_list membership test as the qualifier precedent. 03b0 uses it to
    refute its own objection: "LiteLLM's provider_list is explicitly lazy-loaded with the comment 'to
    avoid importing LlmProviders at import time' — the same constraint I have, already solved. So the
    objection was mine, not the architecture's."
  - eb58 diverges on exactly one point: api_key inline (see D32).
WARNING: the "documented to drift" claim carries NO citation — no URL, issue number, or measurement.
Soften it, or lean on the OpenHands model_features.py observation, which IS concrete.

## 2.2 A gateway fronting Bedrock (PR #121) — REJECTED for native Bedrock
Epic: "Alternative rejected: gateway-only Bedrock (PR #121's approach). It requires every operator to
stand up and accredit a proxy, and gives up caching, thinking, native structured output, and the retrying
transport."
THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT, and it appears only in the epic's Context — a gateway "records a `model` string in
the SIGNED verdict sidecar that no longer names what actually answered."
EVIDENCE the native path delivers what the gateway gives up (2932, real AWS):
  us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 attempt 1 cache_write=4017 cache_read=0; attempt 2 cache_write=0
  cache_read=4017; reproducible. And a full `rebar review-plan` against real Bedrock produced a
  well-formed verdict — "the canary is a single text-mode call, whereas review-plan drives the FULL
  agentic gate on Bedrock."
FOLLOW-THROUGH (7fe2): the gateway option was not merely rejected — the residual gateway/* family is now
STAMPED best_effort. See 2.4.

## 2.3 provider.startswith(...) prefix matching — REJECTED for registry membership. THE GUARD, NAMED.
THE GUARD TEST: tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:119
  test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching
Docstring (:120-121): "f184's attested criterion. The exact-id table must use set/dict membership, never
prefix matching — which also keeps it from speculating about unmeasured models."
Mechanism (:122-138): ast.parse's capabilities.py's own source, collects every ast.Call whose func is an
ast.Attribute with attr in {"startswith","endswith"}, asserts the list is empty. Assertion message is
precise about scope: "capabilities.py must not prefix-match provider names (asserted on real calls, not on
text — a comment naming the banned pattern is fine)". SCOPE: capabilities.py ONLY.
THE EVIDENCE THAT THE GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATIVE — 7fe2 verbatim: "THE ATTESTED ARCHITECTURAL
GUARD HELD — checked FIRST, because this ticket was ORIGINALLY FILED proposing
provider.startswith('gateway/'), which would have violated it: grep -c 'startswith'
src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py => 0 (zero, in code AND comments)... The prefix approach originally filed was
NOT implemented. Registry membership, zero exceptions, holds."
=> CLEANEST POSSIBLE ADR DEMONSTRATION: the ticket was filed with a one-line prefix match, and the guard
   forced a frozenset of five exact ids instead. Record it as "the filed one-liner was rejected on an
   architectural invariant, not on correctness."
COMPANION GUARDS (all verified present):
  test_bedrock_provider.py:103 test_f184_predicate_contract_is_untouched — pins every _REBAR_OVERRIDES
    predicate to a one-argument ModelProfile signature, so the table cannot be widened into a name-keyed
    dict.
  test_verdict_provenance.py:278 test_gateway_tier_is_not_decided_by_the_provider_names_shape — mygateway,
    openai-gateway, gateway, gateway-anthropic all stay first_class. The anti-prefix rule asserted as
    BEHAVIOUR; 7fe2 notes it "passed PRE-fix in the RED run, so it is genuinely unchanged rather than
    newly satisfied."
  test_verdict_provenance.py:235 test_the_enumerated_gateway_set_matches_the_config_registry_exactly — the
    drift pin; its docstring explicitly says "This test may use startswith; the ban is on capabilities.py,
    not on its tests."
  test_provider_qualifier.py:288 test_the_static_set_does_not_drift_from_the_runtime_registries — asserts
    set(session._builders) <= KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES. One-directional BY DESIGN: "so that a future rebar
    builder for a name pydantic-ai does not enumerate is not a failure."
  test_provider_qualifier.py:203 test_known_provider_names_is_exactly_the_registry — pins the 24-name
    literal.
ONE SURVIVING EXCEPTION — name it rather than claiming a clean sweep:
  src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:54 — `if not web or not resolved.startswith("anthropic"):` in
  _anthropic_web_search_capabilities, called from runner.py:417-419. A LIVE provider-name prefix match on
  a decision path, OUTSIDE capabilities.py, so the AST guard does not cover it.
  NOT decision paths (report as such): providers.py:4/:184 docstrings describing the REMOVED branch;
  config.py:274 model-name (not provider-name) inference, reached only after the membership test fails;
  evals/provider_parity.py:479 harness helper.
HONESTY NOTE: grep for "7b22" across src/, tests/, docs/, .rebar/ returns NOTHING. The decision is
attributed in-code as "f184's attested criterion" (capabilities.py:374, test_bedrock_provider.py:120) and
"epic 061c's standing decision" (capabilities.py:375).

## 2.4 A gateway run stamped first_class — REJECTED; gateways are best_effort
7fe2 defect: "KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES admits gateway/anthropic, gateway/bedrock, gateway/google-cloud,
gateway/groq and gateway/openai, and these are LIVE... A gateway/anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 run carries NO
base_url, so it is stamped first_class with endpoint_host: None — even though every byte traversed
Pydantic's AI Gateway, an intermediary that can rewrite the request."
Why it matters more here: "rebar SIGNS verdicts and stamps the tier... A gateway run stamped first_class
misrepresents provenance in a signed artifact."
THE EVIDENCE, as cited: "Third-party evidence that gateways do rewrite silently: the Vercel AI Gateway has
been documented silently downgrading Anthropic's 1-hour prompt cache
(danielternyak.com/articles/vercel-ai-gateway-downgrades-anthropic-prompt-cache)."
CITE WITH CARE: a SINGLE third-party blog post, no scheme, no date, no corroboration, and it is about
VERCEL's gateway, not Pydantic's. It supports "gateways can silently rewrite"; it does NOT evidence that
Pydantic AI Gateway does.
ALSO REJECTED HERE: back-filling endpoint_host for a gateway. "endpoint_host reports what was CONFIGURED,
so synthesising a hostname from a provider id would report a value nobody set." capabilities.py:420-426;
guard test_verdict_provenance.py:297.

## 2.5 A cross-provider FallbackModel to direct Anthropic — REJECTED for the production cutover
eb6e: "No cross-provider fallback. A FallbackModel to direct Anthropic would keep landings flowing during
a Bedrock outage, but it would also mask exactly the failures this cutover exists to surface, and it would
keep an Anthropic key in SSM that the cutover otherwise retires." And: "Alternative rejected:
FallbackModel to direct Anthropic — masks the signal the dogfooding is for, and a persistently degraded
Bedrock could run unnoticed behind a silent fallback."
THE REPLACEMENT CHAIN (four mechanisms, all cited to code): "the existing tenacity transport retry absorbs
transient faults, the existing fail-closed VOTER_ERROR path (review_bot/voter.py:69) handles hard failure,
a CloudWatch alarm fires on VOTER_ERROR, and a documented one-line kill switch (REBAR_LLM_MODEL back to
anthropic:...) is the human recovery path."
VERIFIED LIVE: the chain "is already built and shipped by story S4b (epic d251)" — alarm
rebar-gerrit-voter-errors in infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf, metric rebar/host:voter_errors published
by infra/scripts/observability.sh §4, runbook infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:110. "VERIFIED LIVE, not
just present in source: describe-alarms returns StateValue: OK with a FRESH datapoint."
THE COST IS STATED, NOT HIDDEN: "if Bedrock degrades, landings stop until a human runs the kill switch."
CRUCIALLY — a cross-provider fallback would happen AUTOMATICALLY today, and that is treated as a BUG:
  eb6e: "ESCALATION CROSSES PROVIDERS. models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6')
  returns [('claude-sonnet-4-6','anthropic'), ('claude-opus-4-8','anthropic')] — BARE ids that infer to
  provider 'anthropic'. On a context-limit error a Bedrock run silently escalates to DIRECT ANTHROPIC."
  (Self-flagged: "confirmed from the function, not observed live.")
  eb58: "lookup is a SUBSTRING match ('if n in model')... but it RETURNS the bare Anthropic name, so a
  Bedrock run that escalates would silently jump to DIRECT ANTHROPIC opus. That is a second split-brain."
  7de4 fixed it, framing it as "the founding defect of epic 061c on a second, independent code path."
NOTE the INTRA-provider FallbackModel was ACCEPTED (cc33): model_classes.py:388. So the rejection is
specifically CROSS-provider fallback for the production cutover, not fallback per se.
PROCESS ARTIFACT worth an ADR line: the kill-switch variable was raised -> WITHDRAWN -> REINSTATED across
three comments. "This is the second flip on it, so the sequence is recorded rather than tidied... I had
checked the repo's six precedents and NOT the parent's plan — the wrong authority for this question."

## 2.6 A long-term Bedrock API key in SSM — REJECTED for the instance role
9249 verbatim: "Alternative rejected: a long-term Bedrock API key in SSM. It fits the existing
fetch-secrets.sh pattern with no IAM change, but AWS's own guidance restricts long-term Bedrock API keys to
development and experimentation and recommends roles with short-lived credentials in production; Wiz
documented such keys appearing in public repositories within two weeks of launch. Trading working
short-lived role credentials for a long-lived bearer token is the wrong direction on a box that already
has an instance role."
Argument shape: (a) it would have been CHEAPER; (b) vendor guidance; (c) an empirical leak observation;
(d) the directional argument. WARNING: (b) and (c) are UNCITABLE as written — see Part 4.
ALSO REJECTED: "a host-side credential broker minting short-lived credentials into the container... a
bespoke component to build, operate, and secure for a problem the instance role already solves."
AND: "Explicitly NOT doing iptables containment. An earlier draft proposed blocking 169.254.169.254 from
non-bot container networks. That is not implementable here — there are no per-container networks to block
between — and it would break opcert, which depends on IMDS."
STATIC LONG-LIVED KEYS are rejected on the CI arm separately (f124): mechanism must be OIDC federation,
"reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path"; static keys "would put a durable AWS credential in CI to
save a one-time role setup."

## 2.7 "Presence of verifications maps to block" — REJECTED in the parity scorer (ed82)
THIS WAS THE PLAN REVIEWER'S OWN SUGGESTED FIX, AND IT WAS REJECTED. ed82 verbatim: "The plan review that
surfaced this bug proposed 'treat a non-empty verifications list as block'. I checked the spec before
implementing it and did NOT take that route, because it would introduce a second defect:
code-review-verify.eval.yaml header: 'Per the T8-advisory contract it is scored on PRESENCE of
verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK verdict... either way the verifier must emit a graded answer set.'
dataset comment: 'the gating scorer is presence-based, so the verifier must emit verifications for both.'
BOTH cases — V-real-defect (gold block) and V-clean-rename (gold advisory) — are REQUIRED to emit a
non-empty list. Mapping presence to block would fix the recall miss and simultaneously score the CLEAN
case as a block, manufacturing a FALSE ACCEPT. The arm carries no polarity, so no adapter can derive one.
Exclusion — the reviewer's stated alternative — is the correct remedy."
Mechanism: "_verdict_decision (imported by provider_parity.py:52 so the two cannot drift) keys only on
verdict == 'FAIL' or a non-empty findings. The verifier emits neither."
Empirical confirmation: "V-real-defect has label: 'block' with v1.decision == v2.decision == 'advisory',
valid: true, errored: false, on BOTH slots."
CHOSEN REMEDY: POLARITY_FREE_SOLVERS = frozenset({"code-review-verify"}) at provider_parity.py:101,
excluded in solver_arm :172, kept SEPARATE from AGENTIC_SOLVERS deliberately: "that set excludes ops
gate_config cannot reach, this one excludes a scorer with no decision to compare. Collapsing them would
lose a reason, and a future reader deleting the 'redundant' set would silently re-admit mis-scored cases."
Rows RETAINED in the artifact for provenance, dropped only from SCORING: "deleting them would discard live
evidence." scoring_note in each slot.
THE HEADLINE FOR THE EPIC: "the mis-scored case was the ONLY recall miss on the BEDROCK arm, on BOTH
slots. Bedrock's true recall is 1.000, not the 0.929 recorded here. The bug was UNDERSTATING the Bedrock
arm."

## 2.8 The prompt-cache breakpoint remedy — REJECTED as WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION (f81d)
f81d closed WONT-FIX, class plan_defect — "the design/plan itself was wrong. The reported BEHAVIOUR was
real and is confirmed; what was wrong was this ticket's prescribed remedy."
THE DISPROOF, read off pydantic-ai source rather than estimated, verbatim: "Both options the description
weighs place the breakpoint AFTER the entire message list: anthropic_cache_messages ->
_apply_message_cache_control (anthropic.py:1770-1795): 'Apply per-block cache_control to the last content
block of the LAST MESSAGE.' anthropic_cache (automatic) -> _build_automatic_cache_control (ibid.
1719-1736)... On Bedrock/Vertex it degrades to _apply_per_block_caching_fallback, which calls the SAME
_apply_message_cache_control. So under either option the marked span ENDS with the per-call-unique tail...
A cache entry whose span always ends in unique bytes is WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. It can never be read,
on either site. The guard the description asks for would therefore have to exclude BOTH sites, which makes
the change inert rather than merely narrow."
ECONOMICS: "implementing the prescribed fix would convert both calls from full price to full price PLUS
the 1.25x write premium — a net LOSS."
STRONGER THAN THE AC ASKED FOR: "the recoverable saving is ZERO, established at MECHANISM level, which is
stronger than the cross-run hit-rate estimate the criterion asked for."
A PREMISE THE TICKET ITSELF HAD ASSERTED WAS DISPROVEN: "the finders' entry is keyed on a system block of
shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body, while the coach's system block is its own stance prose. The two
requests diverge at the FIRST SYSTEM BYTE." Plus: "coach_notes is a SINGLE step behind branch: coach_gate
— one call per gate run, not a loop. There is no second coach call within the 5-minute TTL."
enrich/ticket-digest written down as PERMANENTLY out of scope so nobody "completes" the fix.
WHAT A REAL FIX WOULD REQUIRE (recorded, not implemented): pydantic_ai.messages.CachePoint
(messages.py:692, honoured anthropic.py:1234) is the only mechanism that can put a breakpoint MID-message
— "a RunRequest content-list change, which the description explicitly notes today's design avoids" — plus
a plan-review-wide shared-prefix redesign.
ACCEPTED END STATE: "the two sub-calls still request caching and receive none. That is now a KNOWN,
MEASURED, ACCEPTED cost with a recorded reason."
Other hypotheses rejected, each with its disproof: "'No breakpoint is placed' — REJECTED: the captured
request shows cache_control on system[0]"; "'The prefix is unstable between calls' — REJECTED twice:
cache_write=0 means no write was ever ATTEMPTED"; "'Provider-side caching unavailable' — REJECTED: finders
cached in the same process, same provider."

## 2.9 A shared automatic cache key across both arms — REJECTED (dd27)
"MIND THE PROVIDER ASYMMETRY — this is the trap: Bedrock has NO bedrock_cache automatic key. LangChain hit
exactly this (langchain#37042): AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware regressed on Bedrock in 1.4.1 because it
switched to top-level automatic caching, which Bedrock rejects with 'cache_control: Extra inputs are not
permitted'. So the two arms need different keys, not one shared setting." capabilities.py:475-484.

## 2.10 Alternatives rejected around the parity harness (0d76)
- A CI job — REJECTED on grounded IAM terms: "the Bedrock grant in iam_s7.tf:57-72 is attached to the
  Gerrit INSTANCE role, and the only GitHub-OIDC role, rebar-terraform-plan, is ReadOnlyAccess — so a CI
  arm would first require a new Bedrock-capable OIDC role, which is unfunded work outside this story."
  Second independent reason: "~3,200 calls. At concurrency 1 that is roughly 9 hours wall clock, which
  EXCEEDS the 6-hour GitHub-hosted job limit." Regression-pinned at provider_parity.py:368.
- An Anthropic-vs-Anthropic noise-floor control run — REJECTED TWICE by the operator, with the consequence
  stated honestly: "without it we cannot say whether 'zero decision flips' is achievable by ANY provider
  pair, including Anthropic against itself."
  WHAT LATER MADE IT UNNECESSARY — corroboration from already-paid-for data: "ticket c403's measurement
  found relation labels shifting on 6 of 12 ordered pairs BETWEEN BUILDS OF IDENTICAL CODE... A zero-flip
  bar across two different models presumed a determinism that does not exist."
- parallel_run_and_diff as the repeat mechanism — REJECTED with a code fact: "'averaged over the N
  repeats' is prose, not behaviour: parallel_run_and_diff runs each item exactly once per runner with no
  repeat loop and no averaging."
- REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES as the corpus cap — REJECTED: "it truncates dataset[:12] per spec and would
  decapitate the largest gold sources" (plan-review-finder 42 cases, container 24).
- A paired real `rebar review-plan` run as the instrument — REJECTED: "RunRequest carries no model-class
  field, so a single-prompt eval case resolves cfg.model and nothing else."
- min_gold was NOT lowered — parity_report called with its default 20.
- A budget guard — DEFERRED: "useful during high-use development, not in production."

## 2.11 Alternatives rejected on the seam and the record
- 7468: an elif chain in run() (PR #121's shape) — "keeps provider knowledge smeared across the runner...
  leaves no place to attach the capability lookups S2 needs"; a bare build_model() bypassing infer_model —
  "abandons the upstream hook, so rebar would own provider-string resolution forever"; a mutable
  out-parameter to smuggle the client back — "an unnamed side channel with no ownership story."
- f184: PR #121's force_prompted: bool — "a per-call-site patch that grows one argument per capability per
  provider, and it encodes the answer at the caller rather than at the model." Proof: grep force_prompted
  is empty.
- f184: a rule derived purely from flags was TRIED AND MEASURED WRONG — "supports_json_schema_output and
  not supports_thinking looks elegant and reproduces Anthropic and OpenAI correctly, but it was tested
  against every provider in today's _NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS and BREAKS TWO: gemini-2.5-flash has
  supports_thinking=True (would lose NativeOutput) and groq has supports_json_schema_output=False."
- dc0d: branching on cfg.base_url BEFORE provider inference — "makes base_url silently override an
  explicit REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER, contradicting rebar's own documented recipe, and adds a fourth
  implicit provider selector."
- 343b: REFUSING to sign off-tier verdicts — "It gives a stronger guarantee but breaks local development
  without a first-class provider key, which weakens exactly the contributor on-ramp docs/plan-review-
  gate.md depends on." And REPLACING the model string with the structured object — "a breaking payload
  change requiring a compatibility gate and a migration for zero added information."
- 343b: carrying provenance through coverage['usage'] — rejected with a code fact: "It is DROPPED, and one
  layer EARLIER than expected. sizing.usage_record builds each per-call record from the runner result's
  _usage SUB-DICT only... all five mint sites pass only the usage dict."
- eb58: a second scalar REBAR_LLM_VERIFIER_MODEL — "Rejected as knowingly short-lived." Provider-
  qualifying the ladder in gate YAML — "hard-codes one provider into the gate definition, which is exactly
  what makes today's ladder non-portable." A new `class:` step key — "would fork the step schema and make
  'model: standard' vs 'class: standard' a silent ambiguity." Load-time class resolution — "would freeze
  the wrong value in a long-lived process and would not be visible to provider_provenance."
- eb6e: BOTH single-scalar cutovers rejected, WITH MEASUREMENT: "us. AND global. opus-4-5 report
  cache_read=0 / cache_write=0 while billing full input; us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 caches. An
  opus-everywhere cutover also loses caching SILENTLY. Conversely a sonnet-everywhere cutover silently
  DOWNGRADES Pass-1 from opus — a finder-quality regression no existing test would catch. So both
  single-model cutovers are wrong, in opposite directions."
- eb6e: cfg.bedrock_model_id / REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID as a second knob — "is parsed from env and
  documented in docs/env-vars.md:55 but is READ BY NOTHING... dead config as landed by S3." (Deleted per
  ticket 281f.)
- 5267: google-gla/google-vertex/vertexai — "pydantic-ai 1.107.1 emits a deprecation warning for these
  prefixes and REMOVES them in v2.0, so choosing one would re-introduce a scheduled break." And directly
  relevant to 7b22: "Adding google_genai to KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES — rejected: it makes a name that neither
  pydantic-ai nor rebar can build a first-class member... 7b22 must not lock that choice in." (7b22
  complied.)
- 48b3: reading the real context window from the model profile — REJECTED ON AN ABSENCE: "ModelCapabilities
  exposes native_structured_output, prompt_cache_style, supports_thinking and supports_temperature — there
  is no context-window field. The same absence is already recorded in-tree at verify.py:278-281."
- 55bc: automatic prune() on sidecar write paths removed; merge-safe bounded retention DEFERRED to
  475e-9b99-9085-4b2d, with the consequence recorded: "sidecar event files grow unbounded per ticket."
- db7f (-> ADR 0058): every sub-800 and hard-coded-800 LOC ceiling in seam tests deleted. Anti-fragmentation
  FLOORS (100) KEPT — "a different rule in the opposite direction... not a duplicate of the gate."
- df2c: its own fix RETIRED UNLANDED, superseded by 0347: "0347's coverage is a STRICT SUPERSET... the
  deferral is BOUNDED (3 attempts, then an escalated -1 plus a VOTER_ERROR), whereas this ticket's ABSTAIN
  never escalated and would have left a permanently broken bot silently vote-less forever."

ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 3/4: OPERATIONAL FINDINGS · DOC CORRECTIONS · THE TIER MODEL

## 3.1 The IMDS hop-limit constraint — AND THE CRUCIAL CORRECTION
WARNING: THIS TICKET'S FRAMING IS WRONG ON ONE POINT. The contingency NEVER FIRED. No metadata_options
terraform change was made, and no ADR 0046 entry was written.
The constraint as stated (9249): "main.tf:50-54 sets http_tokens = 'required' and leaves
http_put_response_hop_limit unset (default 1, which normally blocks the extra Docker-bridge hop), and
pyproject.toml's reviewbot comment says the journald fallback exists because 'in-container IMDS is
unreachable' — yet docker-compose.yml:157-158 documents the opcert container fetching SSM keys with boto3
where 'the instance profile supplies the credentials via IMDS', which only works if IMDS IS reachable."
=> THE MANIFESTATION WAS A DOCUMENTARY CONTRADICTION IN THE TREE, NOT A CREDENTIAL FAILURE.
Default position taken BEFORE measuring: "The opcert container's working instance-profile SSM fetch is
direct evidence, and it is stronger evidence than the pyproject.toml remark."
The contingency was pre-decided IN FULL so nothing was deferred to the executor, with a bounded-exposure
argument: "docker-compose.yml defines no networks: section, so gerrit, review-bot, and opcert already
share one default bridge, and all three are first-party rebar components that already receive
instance-role-derived secrets through the .env that fetch-secrets.sh writes. Raising the hop limit
therefore widens reach to containers that are already inside the same trust boundary."
THE MEASUREMENT (operator-attested, SSM on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, 896586841071/us-east-1):
    === AC1 — IMDSv2 token request from INSIDE the review-bot container ===
      http_status=200   token_len=56   role=rebar-gerrit-instance-role
"DECISION RECORDED: this selects the IAM-only path; the hop-limit contingency did NOT fire, so the
conditional HttpPutResponseHopLimit == 2 criterion is vacuous."
THE CONTAINMENT IS "MEASURE FIRST, CHANGE NOTHING." Honest ADR content: IMDS IS reachable from containers
at hop limit 1 (measured); the exception was pre-authorized with a bounded-exposure rationale and was NOT
needed; the standing exposure fact is the flat single-bridge compose topology.
AND THE pyproject.toml COMMENT WAS WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN CAUSE (a574): "the review bot's CloudWatch voter
metrics (voter.py:95/110/151/215) silently no-op for the SAME missing-region reason. Their comments blame
IMDS reachability, which the above shows is not the cause." Cite as an example of an unevidenced in-tree
comment misdirecting a design.

## 3.2 Bedrock region resolution — VERIFIED, with a subtler reason than expected
(a) IMDS supplies NO region. 9249: "inside that container boto3.session.Session().region_name is None and
    boto3.client('bedrock-runtime') raises NoRegionError... So region discovery does NOT come from
    instance metadata here: raising the hop limit would fix credential reachability and still leave the
    region unresolved. The two concerns are INDEPENDENT... Every Bedrock probe in this epic passed an
    explicit region_name argument, which is why this stayed invisible until it was measured directly."
    Mechanism (a574): "botocore's IMDSRegionProvider is wired ONLY into the smart-defaults path
    (defaults_mode=auto), so a reachable IMDS supplies credentials but never a region."
(b) rebar's own knob alone was NOT sufficient. a574 verbatim: "setting ONLY REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION was
    NOT sufficient. I set it, restarted the service, and boto3 STILL raised NoRegionError — because that
    is rebar's OWN knob and boto3 has never heard of it. rebar's path worked (it threads the value into
    BedrockProvider) while every other AWS caller in the image stayed region-less. AC4's insistence on a
    BARE boto3 client with no explicit region is exactly what exposed the conflation. Both vars are now
    set and they are NOT interchangeable."
(c) AWS_REGION ALONE DOES NOT WORK on this botocore. MEASURED: "AWS_REGION=us-east-1 only ->
    Session().region_name is None -> NoRegionError; AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=eu-west-1 -> region_name ==
    'eu-west-1'. botocore's session-variable table (configprovider.py:74) maps region to
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION only." VERSION-SCOPED: boto3/botocore 1.43.58 — carry that qualifier.
    Two rebar docstrings were factually wrong and were corrected: bedrock_model.py:50-51, config.py:19-20.
(d) THE EXCEPTION THAT ESCAPES IS NOT NoRegionError: "pydantic-ai already catches botocore's NoRegionError
    at providers/bedrock.py:463 and re-raises pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError... The REAL defect is
    narrower: UserError is NOT a subclass of rebar's LLMError/LLMUnavailableError, so no except LLMError
    handler in rebar catches it — including the review bot's fail-closed path."
(e) The preflight oracle is boto3.session.Session().region_name, NOT env sniffing: "a read-only property...
    measured at 0.002s. Hand-rolling os.environ.get('AWS_REGION') would report a region that boto3 then
    refuses." bedrock_model.py:78.
(f) SEVERITY: "That is a HARD failure at client construction, before any model call, and story eb6e ships
    the cutover with NO cross-provider fallback. So flipping REBAR_LLM_MODEL to bedrock:... without also
    setting a region takes the LLM-Review gate down for every landing rather than degrading it."
(g) DURABILITY: "/opt/rebar is a DEPLOYED COPY, not a git checkout, so the in-place edit alone would have
    been reverted by the next deploy."
(h) THE STRONGEST METHODOLOGICAL LESSON IN THE EPIC: "the runbook ENCODED THE BLIND SPOT: every probe in it
    passes --region explicitly, so none ever exercised ambient resolution. That is precisely why
    NoRegionError survived an entire epic of Bedrock verification."

## 3.3 Caching and inference profiles — the measured relationship
NOT mutually exclusive; only inference profiles are invokable at all. eb6e: "ON-DEMAND MODEL IDS ARE NOT
INVOKABLE AT ALL, so the on-demand-vs-profile comparison the hedge contemplates is moot." And "PROMPT
CACHING WORKS WITH A REGIONAL INFERENCE PROFILE: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 measured cache_write=4017
on attempt 1 and cached on attempt 2. They are NOT mutually exclusive."
THIS REFUTES THE ISSUE THE EPIC WAS BUILT AROUND (2932): "This refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381 for
this model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce."
CACHING IS MODEL-DEPENDENT AND FAILS SILENTLY; the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix.
2932: "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 AND global.anthropic... both returned cache_read=0 AND
cache_write=0 on both attempts, with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning.
CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST INFERENCE: I initially attributed this to the global. prefix; a controlled
same-model comparison showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix. This
silent double-billing is the real hazard #4381 is circling."
Hence Decision B (the cache-zero warning) and why it cannot reuse _warn_if_zeroed_usage: "That guard fires
on requests > 0 AND input_tokens == 0 AND output_tokens == 0. The measured Bedrock failure is the OPPOSITE
shape: input_tokens=4029 with cache_read=0 and cache_write=0. The existing predicate never fires."
Also: "us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 with a cachePoint hard-fails: AccessDeniedException: You
invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching."
END TO END THROUGH REBAR (7a79, 19-call gate run): cache_read_tokens=542,723 cache_write_tokens=6,239. Raw
boto3, 29,400-char repeated prefix: sonnet-4-6 cacheWrite=6604 then cacheRead=6604; opus-4-8
cacheWrite=11404 then cacheRead=11404. "pydantic-ai's Bedrock adapter does map
cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens (models/bedrock.py:676-682), so these are real numbers."
THE cachePoint TTL PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECTED (1aa2): "Bedrock's cachePoint block takes an
OPTIONAL ttl that DEFAULTS TO 5 MINUTES — the same default Anthropic's cache_control applies. The TTL is
not missing on Bedrock; it is defaulted, and defaulted to the SAME value... There is no observable
difference to account for, and no per-provider cache tuning is needed. Bedrock additionally offers a
1-hour TTL for some Claude models. It is opt-in and rebar does not request it, so it is not a difference
either. Sources: AWS 'Amazon Bedrock now supports 1-hour duration for prompt caching' (Jan 2026) and the
Bedrock cachePoint API reference." Honest limit: "no gate run exercises a gap LONGER than 5 minutes... the
runs confirm the lifetime is not shorter than a gate run; they do not probe expiry."
=> SUPERSEDES the "Bedrock cachePoint carries no TTL" claim which appears in 0d76 comments 18/19/20, on
   061c's own final comment, and in 1aa2's description. DO NOT CARRY THE OLD VERSION INTO THE ADR.
rebar never writes the raw wire key: grep cachePoint across src/ returns nothing.

## 3.4 Bedrock model-id constraints (the trap set)
- Plain foundation-model ids are refused on-demand: "Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput
  isn't supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile." "Any Bedrock example
  config that omits the us. prefix is broken on arrival."
- list-foundation-models IS A TRAP: "it enumerates on-demand FOUNDATION models, not INFERENCE PROFILES,
  and the us.-prefixed profile id is exactly the form that is not a foundation model."
- global. inference profiles are a valid MEASURED form in 896586841071 — do not pin us. in IAM.
- VERSIONED Bedrock ids break provider qualification (3768): "_resolve_target's 'already
  provider-qualified' test is ':' in model, and a versioned Bedrock id contains a colon in its version
  suffix, so the configured provider='bedrock' was silently dropped." -> bug 03b0. Operational sting: "the
  canonical id is what the AWS console and docs display, so ...-v1:0 is the string an operator will paste."
- THE INVERSE ALSO BITES (8455): unversioned haiku is INVALID on Bedrock; the valid form carries the
  version suffix -> ValidationException: The provided model identifier is invalid.
- temperature is FATAL on some Bedrock models: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 + temperature=0 -> 400
  "'temperature' is deprecated for this model"; identical call without it succeeds. Root asymmetry:
  "_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's models/anthropic.py, NOT in
  models/bedrock.py — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully and the Bedrock path hard-fails."

## 3.5 IAM, account, identity
- Account/region for ALL landed work: 896586841071 / us-east-1.
- THE WRONG-ACCOUNT INCIDENT (2932/0d76), verbatim: "IMPORTANT CORRECTION — my Bedrock measurements were
  taken in a DIFFERENT AWS ACCOUNT AND REGION than this project's infrastructure. I did not check this
  before recording them as findings, and the operator caught it." Wrong place: account 5797...98, region
  us-east-2, IAM user joe_sec with AmazonBedrockFullAccess. "Bedrock model access is enabled per account
  AND per region." Re-measurement was assigned to 0d76/9249 and completed.
- Policy: rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse, inline on rebar-gerrit-instance-role, in a NEW iam_s7.tf (the
  single-owner contract at iam.tf:4-9 forbids editing iam.tf). Actions InvokeModel +
  InvokeModelWithResponseStream. bedrock:Converse deliberately NOT granted: "it is not the action checked,
  and granting an unused action is blast radius for nothing."
- BOTH resource wildcards are load-bearing: region wildcard "because a cross-region inference profile
  invokes the foundation model in its member regions"; the *. profile-prefix wildcard "because global.
  inference profiles are a valid MEASURED form." "The region field is wildcarded; the MODEL is not."

ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 4/4: HONESTY LEDGER, SUPERSESSIONS, AND THE EPIC'S ACTUAL STATE
Read this part BEFORE writing the ADR. It contains corrections to this ticket's own premises, claims the
code does not support, and supersessions that must be got the right way round.

## 6.1 UNEVIDENCED DESIGN CHOICES
1. "WHY THREE MODEL CLASSES" IS NEVER ARGUED ANYWHERE. eb58 offers prior art for the SHAPE (LiteLLM
   aliases, Aider's --model/--weak-model/--editor-model, pydantic-ai FallbackModel) and one in-code
   precedent that distinguishes only TWO tiers (DEFAULT_MODEL = frontier, VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL documented
   as "the decisive NON-FRONTIER model"). No comment defends three over two or four. `trivial`'s only
   appearance in eb58 is as the bottom ladder rung. TREAT "THREE" AS AN UNEVIDENCED CHOICE, or derive it
   from the ladder's three rungs and SAY SO.
2. eb58's "There are few clients today" — the load-bearing half of the REBAR_LLM_MODEL deprecation
   rationale — has NO count, grep, or inventory.
3. NO alternative NAMES for the three classes (cheap/mid/best, weak/strong) and NO alternative field sets
   for provider_provenance are recorded as considered. The absence of a rejected-naming record is itself
   worth an ADR note.
4. LiteLLM's "normalization layer is documented to drift" has NO URL, issue, or measurement.

## 6.2 UNCITABLE THIRD-PARTY EVIDENCE
5. THE WIZ CLAIM — "Wiz documented such keys appearing in public repositories within two weeks of launch"
   (9249) — no link, date, or report title. It is the EMPIRICAL LEG of the SSM-key rejection.
6. AWS's guidance on long-term Bedrock API keys — paraphrased, no doc URL or section.
7. THE VERCEL AI GATEWAY BLOG POST (7fe2) — bare scheme-less host+path, no read date, single source, and it
   is about a DIFFERENT gateway than the one it is used to justify tiering. (Also: the repo had open CodeQL
   URL-substring alerts 81/82 which may relate to this citation shape.)
8. dd27's Anthropic docs / LangChain middleware / langchain#37042 — cited by path and issue number, no
   URLs, no read date. CONTRAST e3cd, which is the GOLD STANDARD (published URL + read date 2026-08-02,
   brackets explicitly demoted to verification-only). NORMALISE CITATIONS IF CARRIED FORWARD.

## 6.3 CLAIMS MADE IN TICKETS THAT THE CODE DOES NOT SUPPORT
9. THE BEDROCK RETRY/TIMEOUT PARITY CLAIM IS UNBACKED BY CODE. Full detail in Part 3 §5.3. THIS IS THE MOST
   IMPORTANT ITEM IN THIS LEDGER.
10. "A consumer now has the lever to reject an off-tier verdict" (343b) — no consumer built, none named, no
    test. And per Part 3 §5.5 caveat 2 it is not a cryptographically bound lever.
11. "Signed verdicts stamp ... tier" — THE TIER IS IN THE UNSIGNED PAYLOAD. The "second, deliberate
    decision" about entering the signed bytes was explicitly deferred and NEVER TAKEN.

## 6.4 SUPERSESSIONS THE ADR MUST GET THE RIGHT WAY ROUND
12. THE bedrock:Converse REVERSAL (9249). A comment headed "SETTLED ... CONFIRMED" recommended granting
    bedrock:Converse on simulate-custom-policy evidence. It was WRONG, and was reversed by a REAL CALL from
    the instance while only Converse was granted: "AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform:
    bedrock:InvokeModel on ... inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. So the ORIGINAL plan was
    right, and my 'fix' broke it." Also caught at close time: the story VIOLATED ITS OWN single-owner
    contract as landed (iam.tf +47 lines, no iam_s7.tf), remediated in patchset 4.
    GATE OBSERVATION WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: "none of these three were caught by the change's own
    LLM-Review +1 or Verified +1. CI cannot see a plan/code contradiction... The close-time plan-review
    re-run is what caught all three — because it is the only gate that reads the PLAN against the CODE."
13. THE PARITY VERDICT FLIPPED TWICE. DO NOT CITE THE FIRST: 0d76 said "DO NOT claim Bedrock as a
    first-class provider on the strength of this run... REMEDIATE, do not reinterpret" and eb6e held the
    cutover. BOTH were superseded by OD4 and the release verdict.
14. THE cachePoint "NO TTL" CLAIM IS WRONG and appears in FOUR places including 061c's own final comment.
    Corrected on 1aa2 (Part 3 §3.3).
15. eb58's "ONE funnel" KEYSTONE WAS RETRACTED by its own author, with three verified falsifications:
    "model_classes.py imports FROM config.py and its own module docstring — which I wrote one ticket
    earlier — states that config.py must never import it back. I proposed the exact cycle I had just
    prohibited."; "model_ladder BYPASSES resolve_model entirely. VERIFIED in source:
    production_batch_runner.py:93, code_review/batch_runner.py:55"; "The verifier paths bypass it too...
    TWO call sites at xcheck.py:198 and xcheck.py:336 that no plan had enumerated."
16. 3768's verify.py:269 CLAIM WAS RETRACTED — the epic's cleanest methodological quote: "RETRACTED — I
    DEFENDED THIS CLAIM AND IT WAS WRONG... The function body does still contain that expression — which is
    all I actually checked — but it has ZERO production call sites...
    test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers ENFORCES that nothing calls it. So the
    rule is superseded and unreachable, not live. I VERIFIED EXISTENCE AND INFERRED REACHABILITY, WHICH IS
    NOT THE SAME THING." Restated on 0d76: "Existence is not reachability."
17. 3768 ESCALATED ITS OWN PROBLEM STATEMENT: "THE DEFECT IS PRE-EXISTING AND WIDER THAN THIS TICKET.
    verify's model: standard, landed by 172e and NOT part of my change, is ALSO ignored... the code-review
    gate has NEVER honoured a per-step model declaration... 172e closed with this latent." Tracked as b690.
    The honest test post-mortem: "WHY MY 9 TESTS PASSED ANYWAY... Neither asserts THE ENGINE PASSES THE
    TOKEN TO THE RESOLVER DURING A RUN... No mutation could distinguish 'declaration honoured' from
    'declaration ignored', because no test observes the runtime binding."
18. 77ed RETRACTED ITS OWN MITIGATION: "I previously wrote that the mitigation was to raise the rung from
    trivial to standard... That was wrong. Sonnet is itself the result of an unnoticed regression, so
    preserving it would ratify the bug."
19. b690 RETRACTED the "asymmetry lead": "plan-review only LOOKED like it honoured classes because with no
    class table frontier == cfg.model == opus."
20. f81d's floor commentary is SUPERSEDED by e3cd — its 253->7930 bracket was too coarse to detect a 1024
    floor.
21. 7a79 RECLASSIFIED ITS OWN TRIGGERING OBSERVATION: "the originally MEASURED opus-4-5 defect was observed
    at 4029 input tokens, i.e. sub-floor. Under the new contract that specific reading is classified as
    expected rather than a defect." And e3cd then corrected 7a79's global as "over-corrected in the other
    direction."
22. e3cd/7a79 REFRAME the opus caching failure: 7a79: "the cache_read=0/cache_write=0 rebar logs on
    claude-opus-4-8 is NOT a model-capability fact, it is a direct-Anthropic-path fact." BUT eb6e's sweeping
    "Bedrock FIXES 7a79 rather than inheriting it" IS BROADER THAN THE EVIDENCE — contradicted within the
    same ticket set by 0d76 (cache_read=0, cache_write=0 on a Bedrock call at 2857 tokens) and eb6e comment
    1 (us. and global. opus-4-5 both non-caching). THE OPUS-4-5 DATAPOINT IS NEVER RECONCILED.
23. baa8 EXONERATED THE PROVIDER SEAM: "Root cause CONFIRMED — two causes, both TEST-side; the provider seam
    is NOT implicated. Neither b690 nor 03b0 is involved."
24. 03b0's OWN JUSTIFICATION FOR DEVIATING was refuted by OSS research: "MY STATED REASON FOR DEVIATING IS
    ANSWERABLE, and three projects show how... So the objection was mine, not the architecture's." And:
    "THE BIGGEST FINDING — the real fix is GUARD ORDER, and I had not implemented it... Fixing the colon
    test alone left half the bug standing."
25. 5e75's "runner.py < 700" PREMISE WAS SUPERSEDED by db7f/ADR 0058, which makes
    .github/module-size-limit.txt (800) the sole authoritative ceiling. Orchestrator instruction recorded:
    "DO NOT chase the <700 line target... the module-size policy explicitly forbids splitting mechanically
    to hit a number."

## 6.5 THINGS WHOSE EVIDENCE COULD NOT BE FOUND AT ALL
26. THE CLOUDWATCH ALARM ARN AND NUMERIC THRESHOLD. 061c's AC demands "threshold >25% of invocations over a
    15-minute window, 2 consecutive periods" on Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rate, "Evidence: the alarm
    ARN and one forced test notification recorded on S8." WHAT EXISTS on eb6e is a DIFFERENT alarm —
    rebar-gerrit-voter-errors on rebar/host:voter_errors (monitoring_s4b.tf) — with NO ARN, NO threshold, NO
    period, NO evaluation count anywhere, and NO forced test notification recorded. IF THE ADR CITES THE
    ALARM AS THE FALLBACK'S REPLACEMENT, THIS IS A GAP.
27. 061c'S PREMISE THAT "our clients will reach Claude through Bedrock more often than through the direct
    Anthropic API." THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING JUSTIFICATION FOR THE WHOLE EPIC, and NO evidence, survey, or
    citation is offered anywhere in ~40 tickets.
28. THROTTLING AS THE RATIONALE FOR INFERENCE PROFILES. eb6e says "with a cross-region inference profile as
    the throttling mitigation" — ZERO throttle events are reported across ~1,400 parity requests, the 27+5+1
    local-gate calls, or the 19-call plan-review. The EVIDENCED reason is entirely different: on-demand ids
    are refused outright. eb6e already says the hedge should be replaced "with the resolved fact."
29. ed82's Verified +1. The ticket is closed but its final comment ends "Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified
    +1. Will not close before Verified +1." — and no later comment records that it arrived. (NOTE: it DID
    merge as 6c390d7a0a; the comment simply was not updated.)
30. 7a79 AND a574 HAVE ALL AC BOXES UNCHECKED despite status closed — an audit-trail gap in both.

## 6.6 THE STATE OF THE EPIC, SO THE ADR DOES NOT OVERSTATE IT
31. *** THE PRODUCTION CUTOVER HAS NOT HAPPENED. *** eb6e: "No plan review, no claim, no implementation, no
    commit, and THE MODEL FLIP WAS NOT PERFORMED — REBAR_LLM_MODEL untouched, fetch-secrets.sh untouched,
    the Anthropic key still fetched." DO NOT WRITE THE ADR AS THOUGH THE REVIEW BOT RUNS ON BEDROCK.
32. f124 (S10, the CI provider matrix) — "the THIRD of the three permanent provider switches, the other two
    being the repo config / local environment (1aa2) and the AWS review bot (eb6e)."
33. eb6e's SCOPE AND APPROACH ARE KNOWN-STALE TEXT STILL LIVE IN AN OPEN TICKET — its observability.sh
    deliverable already shipped under S4b, and its per-pass model ACs and hard prerequisite on cc33 never
    made it into the description.
34. THE PARITY MEASUREMENT IS A SNAPSHOT ON A STALE BASE. commit 4214516f95a — "This PREDATES 48b3/77ed and
    the 8415/c403 overlap-token work, so the measurement is on that base, not on today's origin/main." No
    re-measurement on current main was performed or approved.
35. metrics.latency_s IN THE COMMITTED ARTIFACT READS 0.0/0.0 after the offline re-score. The real numbers
    survive in the comments and in git at 72f863b5a2. AN ADR CITING THE ARTIFACT RATHER THAN THE COMMENT
    WILL READ THE WRONG NUMBER.
36. 0d76's EPISTEMIC SELF-CRITICISM, worth an ADR line on AC design: "they ask whether the artifact CARRIES
    a metrics block with the required fields, not whether those metrics are CORRECTLY SCORED... an AC that
    checks for the PRESENCE of a measurement cannot detect a measurement that is wrong."
37. 061c's EPIC ATTESTATION IS STALE-CODE: review-plan 061c --status reported 18 DRIFTED dependency files
    (incl. docs/env-vars.md, docs/event-schema.md, docs/llm-framework.md, infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf,
    pyproject.toml) against signing sha 7fc96b277. A FRESH EPIC PLAN REVIEW IS REQUIRED BEFORE CLOSE
    REGARDLESS.
38. 7b22, ed82, a574, 1903, 281f, 3a98 AND STORY 7f86 (with its whole closed subtree e6bd/8229/a49e) ARE NOT
    CHILDREN OF 061c — 7f86 is closed with parent=None. 061c records this: "the epic's real delivered scope
    is wider than its child list shows. One `rebar edit 7f86 --parent=061c...` would reattach the largest
    piece." THE ADR'S OWN SCOPE STATEMENT SHOULD REFLECT DELIVERED WORK, NOT THE CHILD LIST.

## 6.7 TWO META-OBSERVATIONS THAT WOULD STRENGTHEN THE ADR
- The ticket record is unusually honest about its own reversals, and at least FOUR are worth preserving AS
  SUCH: the wrong-account measurement; the "existence is not reachability" retraction; the
  simulator-vs-real-call reversal; and the eb6e durability double-flip with its lesson about checking the
  PARENT PLAN rather than REPO PRECEDENT for a question of deliberate design intent.
- THE SINGLE BEST SENTENCE FOR A "WHY THE BAR CHANGED" SECTION: "My earlier judgement — that the ticket
  could not honestly close as 'Bedrock cleared the bar' — was correct under the OLD criteria; the criteria
  were the problem, not the measurement."

## PROVENANCE OF THIS MATERIAL
Gathered by a read-only research pass on 2026-08-03 that modified no file, touched no ticket, and ran no
gate. Code citations opened and line-verified at HEAD 6c390d7a0a. Raw ticket dumps preserved at
/tmp/adrsrc/*.txt and working notes at /tmp/agent{A,D,E,F}.md (EPHEMERAL — /tmp is not durable; this
comment is the durable copy). Where a claim could not be sourced it is listed in §6 rather than repeated as
fact.
