ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 3/4: OPERATIONAL FINDINGS · DOC CORRECTIONS · THE TIER MODEL

## 3.1 The IMDS hop-limit constraint — AND THE CRUCIAL CORRECTION
WARNING: THIS TICKET'S FRAMING IS WRONG ON ONE POINT. The contingency NEVER FIRED. No metadata_options terraform change was made, and no ADR 0046 entry was written. The constraint as stated (9249): "main.tf:50-54 sets http_tokens = 'required' and leaves http_put_response_hop_limit unset (default 1, which normally blocks the extra Docker-bridge hop), and pyproject.toml's reviewbot comment says the journald fallback exists because 'in-container IMDS is unreachable' — yet docker-compose.yml:157-158 documents the opcert container fetching SSM keys with boto3 where 'the instance profile supplies the credentials via IMDS', which only works if IMDS IS reachable." => THE MANIFESTATION WAS A DOCUMENTARY CONTRADICTION IN THE TREE, NOT A CREDENTIAL FAILURE. Default position taken BEFORE measuring: "The opcert container's working instance-profile SSM fetch is direct evidence, and it is stronger evidence than the pyproject.toml remark." The contingency was pre-decided IN FULL so nothing was deferred to the executor, with a bounded-exposure argument: "docker-compose.yml defines no networks: section, so gerrit, review-bot, and opcert already share one default bridge, and all three are first-party rebar components that already receive instance-role-derived secrets through the .env that fetch-secrets.sh writes. Raising the hop limit therefore widens reach to containers that are already inside the same trust boundary." THE MEASUREMENT (operator-attested, SSM on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, 896586841071/us-east-1):
    === AC1 — IMDSv2 token request from INSIDE the review-bot container ===
      http_status=200   token_len=56   role=rebar-gerrit-instance-role
"DECISION RECORDED: this selects the IAM-only path; the hop-limit contingency did NOT fire, so the conditional HttpPutResponseHopLimit == 2 criterion is vacuous." THE CONTAINMENT IS "MEASURE FIRST, CHANGE NOTHING." Honest ADR content: IMDS IS reachable from containers at hop limit 1 (measured); the exception was pre-authorized with a bounded-exposure rationale and was NOT needed; the standing exposure fact is the flat single-bridge compose topology. AND THE pyproject.toml COMMENT WAS WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN CAUSE (a574): "the review bot's CloudWatch voter metrics (voter.py:95/110/151/215) silently no-op for the SAME missing-region reason. Their comments blame IMDS reachability, which the above shows is not the cause." Cite as an example of an unevidenced in-tree comment misdirecting a design.

## 3.2 Bedrock region resolution — VERIFIED, with a subtler reason than expected
(a) IMDS supplies NO region. 9249: "inside that container boto3.session.Session().region_name is None and
    boto3.client('bedrock-runtime') raises NoRegionError... So region discovery does NOT come from
    instance metadata here: raising the hop limit would fix credential reachability and still leave the
    region unresolved. The two concerns are INDEPENDENT... Every Bedrock probe in this epic passed an
    explicit region_name argument, which is why this stayed invisible until it was measured directly."
    Mechanism (a574): "botocore's IMDSRegionProvider is wired ONLY into the smart-defaults path
    (defaults_mode=auto), so a reachable IMDS supplies credentials but never a region."
(b) rebar's own knob alone was NOT sufficient. a574 verbatim: "setting ONLY REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION was
    NOT sufficient. I set it, restarted the service, and boto3 STILL raised NoRegionError — because that
    is rebar's OWN knob and boto3 has never heard of it. rebar's path worked (it threads the value into
    BedrockProvider) while every other AWS caller in the image stayed region-less. AC4's insistence on a
    BARE boto3 client with no explicit region is exactly what exposed the conflation. Both vars are now
    set and they are NOT interchangeable."
(c) AWS_REGION ALONE DOES NOT WORK on this botocore. MEASURED: "AWS_REGION=us-east-1 only ->
    Session().region_name is None -> NoRegionError; AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=eu-west-1 -> region_name ==
    'eu-west-1'. botocore's session-variable table (configprovider.py:74) maps region to
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION only." VERSION-SCOPED: boto3/botocore 1.43.58 — carry that qualifier.
    Two rebar docstrings were factually wrong and were corrected: bedrock_model.py:50-51, config.py:19-20.
(d) THE EXCEPTION THAT ESCAPES IS NOT NoRegionError: "pydantic-ai already catches botocore's NoRegionError
    at providers/bedrock.py:463 and re-raises pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError... The REAL defect is
    narrower: UserError is NOT a subclass of rebar's LLMError/LLMUnavailableError, so no except LLMError
    handler in rebar catches it — including the review bot's fail-closed path."
(e) The preflight oracle is boto3.session.Session().region_name, NOT env sniffing: "a read-only property...
    measured at 0.002s. Hand-rolling os.environ.get('AWS_REGION') would report a region that boto3 then
    refuses." bedrock_model.py:78.
(f) SEVERITY: "That is a HARD failure at client construction, before any model call, and story eb6e ships
    the cutover with NO cross-provider fallback. So flipping REBAR_LLM_MODEL to bedrock:... without also
    setting a region takes the LLM-Review gate down for every landing rather than degrading it."
(g) DURABILITY: "/opt/rebar is a DEPLOYED COPY, not a git checkout, so the in-place edit alone would have
    been reverted by the next deploy."
(h) THE STRONGEST METHODOLOGICAL LESSON IN THE EPIC: "the runbook ENCODED THE BLIND SPOT: every probe in it
    passes --region explicitly, so none ever exercised ambient resolution. That is precisely why
    NoRegionError survived an entire epic of Bedrock verification."

## 3.3 Caching and inference profiles — the measured relationship
NOT mutually exclusive; only inference profiles are invokable at all. eb6e: "ON-DEMAND MODEL IDS ARE NOT INVOKABLE AT ALL, so the on-demand-vs-profile comparison the hedge contemplates is moot." And "PROMPT CACHING WORKS WITH A REGIONAL INFERENCE PROFILE: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 measured cache_write=4017 on attempt 1 and cached on attempt 2. They are NOT mutually exclusive." THIS REFUTES THE ISSUE THE EPIC WAS BUILT AROUND (2932): "This refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381 for this model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce." CACHING IS MODEL-DEPENDENT AND FAILS SILENTLY; the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix. 2932: "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 AND global.anthropic... both returned cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0 on both attempts, with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning. CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST INFERENCE: I initially attributed this to the global. prefix; a controlled same-model comparison showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix. This silent double-billing is the real hazard #4381 is circling." Hence Decision B (the cache-zero warning) and why it cannot reuse _warn_if_zeroed_usage: "That guard fires on requests > 0 AND input_tokens == 0 AND output_tokens == 0. The measured Bedrock failure is the OPPOSITE shape: input_tokens=4029 with cache_read=0 and cache_write=0. The existing predicate never fires." Also: "us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 with a cachePoint hard-fails: AccessDeniedException: You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching." END TO END THROUGH REBAR (7a79, 19-call gate run): cache_read_tokens=542,723 cache_write_tokens=6,239. Raw boto3, 29,400-char repeated prefix: sonnet-4-6 cacheWrite=6604 then cacheRead=6604; opus-4-8 cacheWrite=11404 then cacheRead=11404. "pydantic-ai's Bedrock adapter does map cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens (models/bedrock.py:676-682), so these are real numbers." THE cachePoint TTL PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECTED (1aa2): "Bedrock's cachePoint block takes an OPTIONAL ttl that DEFAULTS TO 5 MINUTES — the same default Anthropic's cache_control applies. The TTL is not missing on Bedrock; it is defaulted, and defaulted to the SAME value... There is no observable difference to account for, and no per-provider cache tuning is needed. Bedrock additionally offers a 1-hour TTL for some Claude models. It is opt-in and rebar does not request it, so it is not a difference either. Sources: AWS 'Amazon Bedrock now supports 1-hour duration for prompt caching' (Jan 2026) and the Bedrock cachePoint API reference." Honest limit: "no gate run exercises a gap LONGER than 5 minutes... the runs confirm the lifetime is not shorter than a gate run; they do not probe expiry." => SUPERSEDES the "Bedrock cachePoint carries no TTL" claim which appears in 0d76 comments 18/19/20, on
   061c's own final comment, and in 1aa2's description. DO NOT CARRY THE OLD VERSION INTO THE ADR.
rebar never writes the raw wire key: grep cachePoint across src/ returns nothing.

## 3.4 Bedrock model-id constraints (the trap set)
- Plain foundation-model ids are refused on-demand: "Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput
  isn't supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile." "Any Bedrock example
  config that omits the us. prefix is broken on arrival."
- list-foundation-models IS A TRAP: "it enumerates on-demand FOUNDATION models, not INFERENCE PROFILES,
  and the us.-prefixed profile id is exactly the form that is not a foundation model."
- global. inference profiles are a valid MEASURED form in 896586841071 — do not pin us. in IAM.
- VERSIONED Bedrock ids break provider qualification (3768): "_resolve_target's 'already
  provider-qualified' test is ':' in model, and a versioned Bedrock id contains a colon in its version
  suffix, so the configured provider='bedrock' was silently dropped." -> bug 03b0. Operational sting: "the
  canonical id is what the AWS console and docs display, so ...-v1:0 is the string an operator will paste."
- THE INVERSE ALSO BITES (8455): unversioned haiku is INVALID on Bedrock; the valid form carries the
  version suffix -> ValidationException: The provided model identifier is invalid.
- temperature is FATAL on some Bedrock models: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 + temperature=0 -> 400
  "'temperature' is deprecated for this model"; identical call without it succeeds. Root asymmetry:
  "_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's models/anthropic.py, NOT in
  models/bedrock.py — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully and the Bedrock path hard-fails."

## 3.5 IAM, account, identity
- Account/region for ALL landed work: 896586841071 / us-east-1.
- THE WRONG-ACCOUNT INCIDENT (2932/0d76), verbatim: "IMPORTANT CORRECTION — my Bedrock measurements were
  taken in a DIFFERENT AWS ACCOUNT AND REGION than this project's infrastructure. I did not check this
  before recording them as findings, and the operator caught it." Wrong place: account 5797...98, region
  us-east-2, IAM user joe_sec with AmazonBedrockFullAccess. "Bedrock model access is enabled per account
  AND per region." Re-measurement was assigned to 0d76/9249 and completed.
- Policy: rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse, inline on rebar-gerrit-instance-role, in a NEW iam_s7.tf (the
  single-owner contract at iam.tf:4-9 forbids editing iam.tf). Actions InvokeModel +
  InvokeModelWithResponseStream. bedrock:Converse deliberately NOT granted: "it is not the action checked,
  and granting an unused action is blast radius for nothing."
- BOTH resource wildcards are load-bearing: region wildcard "because a cross-region inference profile
  invokes the foundation model in its member regions"; the *. profile-prefix wildcard "because global.
  inference profiles are a valid MEASURED form." "The region field is wildcarded; the MODEL is not."
- Pre-change baseline recorded so the delta is unambiguous: all four actions implicitDeny. "The grant was
  genuinely additive."
- NEGATIVE CONTROL (the least-privilege oracle): "converse to amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 returns
  AccessDeniedException naming bedrock:InvokeModel on the nova ARN — so the Claude-only scope genuinely
  binds."
- Tooling gotchas now in the runbook: aws-cli 2.33.15 on this AMI exposes NO bedrock-runtime streaming
  subcommand ("An unknown subcommand exits printing the CLI help stub, which reads like a failed call");
  SSM AWS-RunShellScript mangles embedded JSON through shell quoting — base64-encode the script; THE
  REVIEW-BOT IMAGE SHIPS NO aws CLI, which made one AC "unsatisfiable by construction."
  --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out is needed for invoke-model's --body, NOT for converse;
  "--inference-config may be passed ONCE only — giving it twice is rejected client-side with Unknown
  options, which looks like an API refusal and is not one."

## 3.6 The Pass-1 archaeology (77ed) — the most consequential silent regression
3,843 plan-review REVIEW_RESULT sidecars by recorded data.model, by day:
  2026-06-24..27: opus 16, 32, 25, 42 | sonnet 0
  2026-06-28:     opus 37            | sonnet 20 (transition)
  2026-06-29 on:  opus 0             | sonnet 87, 78, ... (2,710 sonnet runs since)
"115 opus runs before the change, ZERO after. A total, permanent changeover one day after the commit." Cause: 4beec08a4 (2026-06-27) introduced _verifier_cfg passed as the WHOLE RUN's cfg, and PydanticAIRunner.run then discarded req.config. "git log -L62,66 on plan-review.yaml shows Pass-1 has declared the cheapest rung since the workflow was born and has NEVER ONCE actually run on it." WHY THE LADDER DOES NOT SAVE IT: "pass1_with_ladder escalates on a CONTEXT-LIMIT signal — it is a SIZE ladder, not a quality ladder (its own docstring says so). A plan that fits haiku's 200k window stays on haiku forever." WHY IT IS SILENT — the loud/quiet asymmetry the ADR should state: "The gates fail CLOSED on errors... That is the loud path and it is fine. This is the other kind: a haiku Pass-1 that surfaces fewer grounded findings yields a PASS, which gets signed, and the claim proceeds. The sidecar records only the VERIFIER's model (data.model), never Pass-1's, so it is invisible in the artifacts too." NOT TEST-DETECTABLE: "the offline suite substitutes FunctionModel/FakeRunner for exactly the thing that changes, which is WHICH MODEL a live gate calls." Found by an independent landing-safety assessment. UNRESOLVED ASYMMETRY WORTH RECORDING: "Code-review's Pass-1 finder declares frontier. Plan-review's Pass-1 declares trivial. Both are finders that generate blocking findings. That asymmetry may be deliberate, but it has never been effective, so it has never been evaluated."

## 3.7 The bypass census (afeb) — the epic's severity-setting measurement
Config B (classes on Bedrock, cfg.model left bare-Anthropic):
  llm/overlap/judge.py:46            overlap-judge   18 calls  anthropic BYPASS
  llm/enrich.py:81                   ticket-digest    1 call   anthropic BYPASS
  llm/operations.py:177              ticket-quality   1 call   anthropic BYPASS
  llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:571 code-novelty    1 call   anthropic BYPASS
"overlap-judge DOMINATES plan-review traffic — 18 of 23 calls. An operator who cuts over by configuring the three classes leaves the MAJORITY of plan-review traffic on direct Anthropic." "ticket-digest IS THE MOST INSIDIOUS... enrich_drain.maybe_drain is called from _store/event_append.py:609 and _store/push.py:295, so it runs on the ticket store WRITE PATH... It therefore sends ticket content to direct Anthropic during routine store operations, with no gate invocation and nothing in a verdict to reveal it." Framing: "Bedrock is normally chosen for data-residency, procurement or contractual reasons." THE TWO-CONFIGURATION METHODOLOGY INVARIANT — MUST NOT BE REDISCOVERED: "Config B — does every call honour the CLASS configuration? (found 4 that do not). Config A — is any provider HARDCODED past configuration entirely? (found none). Config A alone is necessary but NOT sufficient: it would have passed even with every bypass site unfixed... Anyone re-running this later should run BOTH, or the result is a false clean." Related (b690): "With no model_classes configured, frontier resolves to the built-in claude-opus-4-8 — which IS cfg.model — so a frontier-declaring step runs on opus whether or not the declaration is honoured." => EVERY LIVE PROBE IN THIS EPIC MUST USE A DISCRIMINATING CLASS TABLE.

## 3.8 Observability invariants (for whoever reads a usage log next)
- REBAR_USAGE_LOG is OPT-IN (usage_log.py:29); this cost a criterion on 77ed.
- It is JSONL, not key=value: "usage_log.py:315 writes json.dumps(row) + '\n'. A model= grep matches
  nothing." And a whole-log grep for bedrock:<model> OVER-COUNTS because verdict-JSON fields match too —
  "it told me 4 when the truth was 1."
- step and model_class come from a ContextVar (b690) WHICH RAW THREADS DO NOT INHERIT (8415): "If overlap
  judging is parallelized with a thread pool and the binding is left outside the pool, every judge call
  silently loses its step/model_class attribution. Bind inside the worker, and assert it in a test."
- op for batch steps is the OVERLAY prompt, not the batch.prompt finder — "so the pass a call belongs to is
  recoverable ONLY from step."
- Every row now carries an explicit outcome (8455); pre-8455 rows must be read row.get("outcome","ok").
- AN EMPTY USAGE LOG IS NOT EVIDENCE NO CALL WAS ATTEMPTED (baa8).
- rebar writes ONE usage row per run() aggregating all HTTP calls, with "requests": N (dd27).

## 3.9 Module-size governance (db7f -> ADR 0058), quoted because it IS the ADR rationale
1. "Governance inversion. The 800 cap is deliberately LOCKED. The stricter bounds that actually bind these
   files are bare literals in test files any contributor can edit. The tightest constraint is the least
   governed one."
2. "It breaks the refactors it exists to encourage. A multi-commit decomposition necessarily passes through
   intermediate states where the file has not shrunk yet... This has now happened twice on this epic's
   stack (changes 1121/1122 at runner.py 782, and again after a rebase)."
3. "It has already cost a full investigation once. Bug 3a98 was opened for exactly this."
4. "The duplication is self-locking. test_decide_ops_seam.py:127,130 assert that the literal strings appear
   in another test file's SOURCE TEXT."

## 3.10 Evidence-hygiene rules earned the hard way (a strong ADR appendix)
- ASSERT git status --porcelain IS EMPTY before the suite you intend to cite (48b3): "CI CAUGHT A REAL
  DEFECT THAT EVERY LOCAL RUN MISSED — the test edits were never committed... A suite run against a dirty
  tree is not evidence about the commit."
- Never validate a scoped policy with a wildcard-holding identity — and CHECK THE ACCOUNT (9249).
- A SIMULATOR ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION THAN A REAL CALL (9249, the marquee finding): "the policy
  simulator answers 'what does the policy language permit for the action you NAMED', not 'which action does
  the service actually CHECK'. Only a real call distinguishes those two questions." And: "Evidence is only
  as good as its ability to have come out the other way FOR THE REASON YOU CARE ABOUT."
- VERIFICATION THAT ENCODES ITS OWN BLIND SPOT — a recurring pattern worth naming once: a574's runbook
  passing --region everywhere; dd27's confounded arms reading each other's cache inside the 5-minute TTL;
  7a79's pre-existing test pinned at input_tokens=4029, itself sub-floor; e3cd's test passing the floor as
  a literal rather than reading it from capabilities_for. "In every case the GUARD shared the BUG's
  assumption."
- NEGATIVE-FORM ACs PASS VACUOUSLY. a574: "an AC asserting 'a TYPED error, not a bare NoRegionError' is
  already true today and proves nothing." f81d: "A test that merely asserts 'a cache breakpoint exists'
  passes for the wrong reason."
- SELF-REFERENTIAL ACs DEADLOCK THE CLOSE GATE (f81d): "gate 433c turns any self-referential AC into an
  unbreakable deadlock, and the phrasing that causes it — 'the correct outcome is to close this as X' — is
  natural to write when an author wants to pre-authorise a wont-fix."
- The completion verifier reads REPOSITORY FILES ONLY, never git history (5e75, 0d76) — out-of-repo
  criteria must be tagged [operator-attested] or they burn a close cycle.
- The default test selection EXCLUDES the integration tier where some evidence lives (55bc).
- Do not mutate the working tree while a gating suite runs in it (2932).
- LIVE GATE RUNS EXCEED THE 600s STREAM WATCHDOG on a loaded host (1aa2): "Four consecutive agent attempts
  were killed... the failure was structural rather than bad luck. A background job has no watchdog." And:
  "the previous attempt completed its five calls and then died while writing the record — the calls were
  billed and produced nothing durable."
- A 4-char short id is NOT guaranteed unique (afeb).
- Set file_impact BEFORE a review, never after (3768): "An unscoped attestation dies stale-head on EVERY
  commit, and setting file_impact AFTER a review is a material edit that destroys the PASS."
- deps is NOT the blocker list (3768): "Blocking comes from LINK relations. rebar ready is the
  authoritative claimability check."
- Run the repo checkout's build, not a stale global install (343b).

## 3.11 Cost, latency and volume figures worth preserving
- THE AGENTIC COST FINDING (0d76): plan asserted "at most 360 model calls"; measured "~102k input tokens
  and ~8.6 requests PER case-run." Root cause: "the code-review arm is agentic too... Eight of the fifteen
  sampled specs are code-review specs." FINAL ACTUAL: ~1,400 provider requests / ~15.4M input tokens.
- Full parity corpus: 30 enumerated / 28 scored (later 26 after ed82), N=3 epochs, 360 case-runs,
  corpus_digest 9d707f76..., commit 4214516f95a.
- LATENCY: standard slot Bedrock 9.9% FASTER (2484.6s vs 2756.5s); frontier within 0.1%. RETIRES the N=1
  pilot's "~35% slower" hint, which was self-retracted.
- Validity 1.000 both arms both slots over 360 case-runs; runtime error rate 0.000; v2 arms provably
  provider-clean (ZERO non-Bedrock calls across 84/84 case-runs per slot).
- dd27's O(N^2) PROOF: 9 calls / 8 tool turns, total prompt tokens IDENTICAL at 109,02 … [truncated by reconciler]

# S9 — ADR + documentation for the provider seam and the two-tier support policy

## Context / Problem

After S1–S8 rebar has a provider seam, a tier policy, a Bedrock path, and tier-stamped verdicts — none of it
written down. `docs/llm-framework.md:121-143` still describes provider support as "pydantic-ai resolves the
provider from the model string" with no mention of tiers, Bedrock, or what a best-effort provider means for a
signed verdict, and its `:131-133` local-server recipe describes behavior that only becomes true in S4. Without
a recorded decision, the next Bedrock/gateway request reopens the same argument as a one-off, which is the
failure mode this epic exists to end.

## Approach

Write one ADR recording the decisions and, importantly, the rejected alternatives with their evidence: the seam
is pydantic-ai's `provider_factory` hook and capabilities come from `ModelProfile`; two support tiers with
Anthropic and Bedrock first-class; native Bedrock rather than a gateway; LiteLLM rejected as an in-process
dependency but reachable as a proxy; verdicts sign on every tier but stamp the tier. Then bring
`docs/llm-framework.md` in line with what the code now does, including the Bedrock recipe, the tier table, and
what tier means for an attestation consumer.

The ADR also records the two operational findings this epic turned up, so they are not rediscovered: the IMDS
hop-limit constraint and its containment [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67], and the measured relationship between
cross-region inference profiles and prompt caching [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].

**Alternative rejected:** documenting in `docs/llm-framework.md` only. That records the *what* but not the
*why*, and rebar's ADR set is where rejected alternatives live — without them the LiteLLM and gateway options
get re-proposed.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/00NN-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md` (new).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — the provider section (`:121-143`) and the env table (`:224-226`).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated.
- `README.md` — one line if the provider story is summarized there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the ADR exists, is `Accepted`, and names each rejected alternative (in-process LiteLLM, gateway-fronted
      Bedrock, refuse-to-sign off-tier, Bedrock API key in SSM, cross-provider fallback) with the evidence that
      rejected it
- [x] [operator-attested] every runnable command in `docs/llm-framework.md`'s provider section has been executed and produced the
      documented result, confirmed in a ticket comment
- [x] the docs state, for each tier, what is guaranteed (tests, parity) and what a consumer can infer from a
      verdict's stamped tier
- [x] [operator-attested] the documented generator produces NO diff to `docs/env-vars.md`, evidenced by the
      command and its empty-diff output quoted in a comment
